by_scheme.question: is boehmite stable against dehydration to corundum, 2 AlOOH -> Al2O3 + H2O, without electrochemistry? Delta_G at the water standard state, and the water pressure (or activity) below which dehydration is favoured: thermodynamics only, no rate

boehmite_dehydration.reading: a threshold, not a verdict: dehydration of boehmite to corundum is favoured below the water partial pressure (or liquid-referenced activity) given per scheme; the governing value is the expt route. The water activity in the electrolyte is not a sourced key (electrolyte_water_content is a mass fraction and gives no activity without a solvation model), so the threshold is not compared with any state of the cell.

limitations: The electrolyte's own anodic limit (anion or solvent oxidation) is not assessed; it may lie below every limit here.
Solid entropies are neglected in every scheme; for the Al(ClO4)3 exchange there is no entropy bound key (W1's exchange_entropy_bound is stated for Ca(ClO4)2).
The Al(ClO4)3 dfH is one fetched value from a free abstract page; it is not a params key, and its reference temperature is not printed (read as 298.15 K).
Water released by boehmite is taken at 1 bar; trace water in the electrolyte lowers the onsets (water_sensitivity), by an amount that needs a water activity that is not a params key.
Reduction limits use 0 K energies (Li-open); the expt cross-check governs where every product is tabulated.

water.reason: The gases of the oxidation reactions are taken at the 1 bar standard state of the benchmark (O2, CO2); water released by boehmite is treated the same way. With the trace water of the electrolyte (key electrolyte_water_content) the water activity is far below one; that lowers every onset by (n_H2O/n_e) k T ln a_w, so both standard-state onsets bound the onset from above. a_w itself is not a params key (the mass fraction does not give an activity without a solvation model), so the shift is reported as a function, never applied.
